title: All-on-4 vs All-on-6 vs full mouth reconstruction: cost and what the data shows
seoTitle: All-on-4 vs All-on-6 vs Full Mouth Reconstruction: Cost and Data
description: Survival data for All-on-4 and All-on-6, when full mouth reconstruction is the better plan, what Miami practices charge per arch, and how Xiluet does it from $10,000.
author: Dr. Roger Ramos Navarro, DMD
imageAlt: Two jaw models on a lab bench, one with four implant analogs and one with six
answer: All-on-4 and All-on-6 perform almost identically: a 2026 meta-analysis found **98.1% vs 97.5%** implant survival at five years or more. The choice is bone and bite, not success rate. If most of your teeth can be saved, a full mouth reconstruction with crowns and bridges is the better plan. Miami practices publish **$20,000 to $30,000 per arch** for All-on-4; at Xiluet Smiles, All-on-X is **from $10,000 per arch** and full mouth reconstruction is from $10,000.

sections.h2: Three treatments, one question: can your teeth be saved?

blocks.p: People search "All-on-4 vs All-on-6" as if it were the main decision. It is not. The first question is whether your own teeth and roots are worth keeping. If they are, you do not need implants at all. If most of an arch is loose, infected or broken below the gum, no crown will hold, and a fixed implant bridge is the honest answer.

list: **Full mouth reconstruction:** your teeth stay. Every tooth is rebuilt with crowns, bridges or veneers, planned as one case so the bite works. Missing teeth are replaced with bridges.
**All-on-4:** an arch of failing teeth is removed and replaced with a fixed bridge on four implants, the two back ones angled to use the bone you already have.
**All-on-6:** the same fixed bridge on six implants. More support, used when the bite is heavy or the bone is softer.

blocks.p: At Xiluet Smiles, the same doctor plans all three. [Dr. Ramos Navarro](/doctors/dr-roger-ramos-navarro) reviews your photos and X-rays first and tells you in writing which one you need, and why, before you book anything.

sections.h2: What the data shows: All-on-4 vs All-on-6

blocks.p: The evidence is reassuring and a little boring. A [2026 meta-analysis](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0901502726001402) comparing the two protocols found implant survival of 98.1% for All-on-4 and 97.5% for All-on-6 at five years or more, with similar bone loss around the implants. Two extra implants do not buy you a higher success rate.

Longer studies of the All-on-4 concept report 94 to 98 percent of implants and about 99 percent of the fixed bridges still in function at 10 years. The bridge itself is the part that wears: acrylic teeth on a temporary bridge chip and stain, which is why the final bridge is made in zirconia and typically lasts 10 to 20 years.

So when does six make sense? When your CT scan shows soft or thin bone that benefits from spreading the load, when you have a heavy bite or grind, or when the opposing arch is natural teeth or another fixed bridge. Four is the standard protocol for a reason, and it is enough for most patients.

blocks.quote: Four implants or six is a question your CT scan answers, not your budget. We place up to six for the same price because we would rather decide clinically.

sections.h2: When full mouth reconstruction is the better plan

blocks.p: Implants replace teeth. Reconstruction keeps them. If your teeth are worn short from grinding, if old fillings and crowns are breaking one after another, if your bite hurts or your front teeth are chipped and discolored, the roots are usually sound. Removing sound roots to place implants is a bigger surgery, a longer recovery and a worse outcome than crowning the teeth you have.

A reconstruction treats the whole mouth as one plan. Your doctor takes 3D scans and a bite analysis, sets the new bite position, and designs every crown, bridge and veneer together so they meet correctly. Where a tooth is missing, a bridge closes the gap. Where a tooth is hopeless, an extraction and a bridge or, if it serves you better, a single implant is written into the plan before anything starts.

Porcelain and zirconia restorations typically last 10 to 30 years with normal care and a night guard if you grind. Crowns and bridges are also often classed as major restorative work by insurers and may be covered 50 to 80 percent depending on your plan; we give you the codes for your claim. Read more on the [full mouth reconstruction page](/full-mouth-reconstruction-miami).

sections.h2: Cost: Miami ranges vs Xiluet Smiles

blocks.p: Nationally, All-on-4 is quoted at [$15,000 to $30,000 per arch](https://globedentalpractice.com/all-on-4-vs-all-on-6-dental-implants/), with All-on-6 typically $3,000 to $5,000 more. Full mouth reconstruction runs [$15,000 to $40,000](https://thedesignersmile.com/blog/2026/04/02/how-much-is-full-mouth-220384/) for moderate cases and $45,000 to $80,000 or more for complex ones. In Miami, most practices that publish an All-on-4 price quote $20,000 to $30,000 per arch; we found one published entry price below $10,000. These are ranges published by Miami practices in October 2026 and they change.

sections.h2: Why the price can be half of the Miami range

blocks.p: The difference is not the implant brand or a cheaper bridge. It is where the bridge is made. Your surgeon, restorative doctor and ceramist work in the same building. There is no outside lab fee on the temporary bridge or the final zirconia bridge, no shipping, and the shade and shape are checked in person. The same in-house lab is why a reconstruction of 20 restorations can be delivered in 7 business days instead of months of separate appointments.

sections.h2: What to ask before you choose

list: Can my teeth be saved? Ask for the reason, tooth by tooth, in writing.
Is the number of implants decided by my CT scan or by the price list?
What does the package exclude: extractions, grafts, sinus lift, the final bridge, the temporary?
Where is the bridge made, and who adjusts it after I fly home?
What is the warranty, in writing, and what does it cover?

blocks.p: If you want those answers for your own mouth, send three photos. faq.a: Not in terms of success rate. A 2026 meta-analysis found 98.1% implant survival for All-on-4 and 97.5% for All-on-6 at five years or more. Six implants add support for a heavy bite or softer bone. Your CT scan decides.

faq.q: How much does All-on-4 cost in Miami?
faq.a: Most Miami practices that publish a price quote $20,000 to $30,000 per arch. At Xiluet Smiles, All-on-X is $10,000 per arch, or $9,000 cash, for up to six implants and a hybrid fixed bridge. Extractions, grafts and sinus lifts are quoted separately after a CT scan.

faq.q: Do I need implants for a full mouth reconstruction?
faq.a: Not for this package. Missing teeth are replaced with bridges. If an implant would serve you better for a specific tooth, your doctor says so in the treatment plan.

faq.q: Will I be without teeth after All-on-X surgery?
faq.a: No. A fixed temporary bridge is fitted the same day as surgery. You wear it for three to four months while the implants heal, then the final zirconia bridge is made across one week in Miami.

faq.q: How long does a full mouth reconstruction last?
faq.a: Porcelain and zirconia restorations typically last 10 to 30 years with normal care and a night guard if you grind. Ours carry a 5-year written warranty.

faq.q: Does insurance cover any of this?
faq.a: Crowns and bridges are often classed as major restorative work and may be covered 50 to 80 percent depending on your plan. We give you the codes for your claim. Check your plan for implants.
